prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the downward-viewed stairwell landing layout, showing the camera wearer's own torso, arms, and held phone at the bottom (0.2–0.5 m away, within immediate reach), the metal handrail on the right (0.3–0.8 m, also within arm's reach), and a standing person in front and to the upper-left about 1.2–2.0 m away, with a tall bucket (1.5–2.2 m) just to that person's right and the floor surface roughly 1.5–2.0 m below. Across the five frames, the camera wearer turns and shifts slightly leftward toward the adjacent wall, making the bright vertical wall on the left fill the near field (0.2–0.6 m) in frames 4–5 while the other person (cropped above the chest/neck so their head and gaze direction are out of view, with their body facing roughly toward the camera wearer and the stairs) shifts from upper-left to upper-center. Small tools on the landing floor (an angle grinder, hammer, level, and cans within reach of the other person's feet) are barely distinguishable from the dark floor plane in depth, whereas the depth map makes the 3D relief of the elevated handrail, vertical wall, and upright bucket silhouette much clearer than in the cluttered RGB texture. The depth map is unreliable in frame 1 where the left wall and stairwell drop-off merge into a black void, and in frames 2–3 where the floor around the other person's legs is overly dark compared to frame 1.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates the foreground silhouettes of the camera wearer at the bottom (0.2–0.5 m) and the standing person above and in front (1.2–2.0 m, roughly 1.0–1.5 m from the wearer, facing generally toward the camera wearer with their head and upper torso out of frame), clearly separating their overlapping limbs from the cluttered construction floor. It highlights the cell phone held in the camera wearer's left hand at 0.4 m in frame 2, and tracks how the other person's lower body and right arm shift from the upper-left toward the upper-center across the five frames as the camera wearer turns slightly left. However, the map is highly unreliable in both class labels and completeness: it misses the standing person completely in frame 1 and the camera wearer's torso in frame 4, splits the camera wearer's right arm into a separate 'person' instance in frame 5, and misclassifies the bucket (1.5–2.2 m away) as a 'cup' in frame 2 and the angle grinder on the floor combined with the held phone as a 'knife' in frame 4. Nearly all other scene elements—including the handrail within arm's reach on the right, the left wall, the stairs, and the remaining floor tools—are unsegmented.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is almost entirely blank across the five frames, failing to detect any yellow body skeletons for either the camera wearer (0.2–0.5 m at the bottom) or the standing person (1.2–2.0 m in the upper-left to upper-center) due to severe top-down perspective foreshortening and partial framing that cuts off both people's heads and upper bodies. It detects only two isolated magenta hand skeletons: the standing person's hanging right hand in frame 3 (about 1.3 m from the camera wearer, to the left of their legs and roughly 0.5 m above the floor tools) and the camera wearer's raised right hand in frame 5 (about 0.4 m away at the lower right, within arm's reach of the wearer's left hand holding the phone). Where present, these magenta skeletons reveal precise finger articulation and palm orientation—showing the other person's curled fingers in frame 3 and the camera wearer's pinching posture in frame 5—more explicitly than the RGB image. Because all other hands in frames 1–5 and both body skeletons are completely missed, the pose map alone is unreliable for tracking full-body orientation, gaze, or multi-frame spatial trajectories.
